thread.title: Midday Update: Higher Bond Yields Rattle Equity Investors

title: Midday Update: Higher Bond Yields Rattle Equity Investors
text:
Midday Update: Higher Bond Yields Rattle Equity Investors February 02, 2018, 12:54:28 PM EDT By MT Newswires, MT Newswires Shutterstock photo 
The Dow Jones Industrial Average hemorrhaged at Friday's open when the yield on the 10-year Treasury note breached 2.80% after bullish labor market data raised the likelihood for the Federal Reserve to continue raising U.S. interest rates. Led by heavy losses in the energy sector, the Dow and S&P 500 fell to their lowest levels in two weeks. 
The major market averages are all indicated to close the week in the red for the first time in five weeks with the Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite all having their worst week in two years. 
Wall Street was already defensive going into the monthly jobs report with rising global bond yields raising worries about higher borrowing costs and unnerving investors. Quarterly results from tech heavyweights added to the malaise when Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) swung to a loss due to a tax charge, while Apple ( AAPL ) iPhone sales disappointed and current quarter guidance was less than Wall Street expectations. 
Bucking the trend was Amazon ( AMZN ), which crushed estimates and rallied to another all-time high. 
Selling pressure accelerated into the NYSE open when the Labor Department reported an increase of 200,000 in non-farm payrolls and 0.3% gain in average hourly earnings. The data drove the 10-year yield to a four-year high of 2.85% and the Dow below 26,000. 
Friday's remaining data were mixed with the University of Michigan final consumer sentiment index for January revised upward to 95.7 from 94.4 initially, but was still down from 95.9 in December. 
Factory orders surged in December by 1.7% with most of the increase attributed to transportation orders. Excluding this sector, factory orders were up a more modest 0.7%. 
Europe's market averages fell in sympathy with the U.S. with losses magnified by discouraging quarterly results from Deutsche Bank ( DB ) and as an ongoing strike among German auto workers roiled the automotive sector. Losses were pronounced in Germany and France where the DAX and CAC-40 lost almost 2% in value. 
Crude oil was down $0.10 to $65.70 per barrel. Natural gas was up $0.04 to $2.90 per 1 million BTU. Gold was down $9.40 to $1,338.40 an ounce, while silver was down $0.38 to $16.76 an ounce. Copper was down $0.02 to $3.19 per pound. 
Among energy ETFs, the United States Oil Fund was down 1.51% to $13.04 with the United States Natural Gas Fund was down 0.53% to $24.22. Amongst precious-metal funds, the Market Vectors Gold Miners ETF was down 1.71% to 23.23 while SPDR Gold Shares were down 1.06%) to $126.71. The iShares Silver Trust was down 2.46% to $15.85.
